text:
alex: RFC follow-up — proposal: add seed-transfer surge control to the on‑prem airgap path to avoid operator overload during large-scale upgrades. quick sketch:

leslie: curious what you mean by 'surge control' here — rate limit per-operator or per-cluster?

alex: both. per-operator token bucket plus a cluster-level concurrency cap. we should prefer operator-level limits so single noisy operator doesn't blast the whole cluster.

maria: +1. also add an adaptive backoff based on operator queue depth and apply failure rate. keep it simple for MVP: token_bucket_rate, bucket_size, max_concurrent_pushes.

alex: config example (MVP):
```
seed_transfer:
  operator_token_rate: 10 # pushes/sec
  operator_bucket: 30
  cluster_max_inflight: 8
  backoff_base_ms: 500
  backoff_mult: 2
```

sam: how would admin force a critical push (hotfix) if the cluster is throttled? need an override path with audit.

maria: console + CLI override via a signed admin token. override stays valid for X minutes and emits an audit event. probably gated behind RBAC.

alex: agree. override flow: 1) admin requests override -> console issues short-lived signed ticket -> operator accepts ticket and escalates priority for that push. audit log entry required.

upgrade-bot: upgrade-bot: Canary push started to node-group-6 (seed_id=seed-2026-03-21-2) :rocket:

jon: we should expose metrics for this: seed_push_inflight, seed_push_rejected_by_rate, seed_push_override_count, seed_push_backoff_seconds. want SLOs for median resume time.

ops: note: when the seed is signed by customer KMS, operator may need to stall while verifying signatures; that should be treated as a backpressure signal not a hard failure.

alex: good call. tag signature-verify latency as a backpressure source; increase backoff if verify_latency > threshold.

leslie: question: resume semantics after partial-apply failure — do we resume on same operator or requeue to another operator?

alex: prefer resume on same operator up to N retries, then requeue. reason: cache/kv state lives local to operator during apply. fallback to requeue if operator unhealthy.

sam: UX idea: expose a small 'resume token' that operator returns on partial failure. CLI: `seed apply --resume TOKEN` to continue.

alex: demonstration: `seed apply --resume htk-4f3a --operator node-6` (operator will validate token and continue from last chunk).

maria: what about telemetry cardinality? token ids should be hashed before logging.

jon: +1 on hashing. only log truncated hash and status (resume/success/fail).

ops: we should also add a circuit-breaker: if cluster_max_inflight reached and average apply latency grows > X for Y minutes, temporarily stop non-critical pushes and notify SRE.

alex: yep. plan for MVP: implement operator token bucket + cluster inflight counter + admin override + resume token + basic metrics. followups: API for querying operator queue lengths, and a UX flow for prioritized emergency pushes.

leslie: sounds reasonable. timeline?

alex: I'll open a small RFC PR with config knobs and an operator shim draft today, aiming for a prototype next sprint.

maria: tagging myself to review the operator shim. :+1:

sam: I'll draft CLI changes for the override and resume flags.

upgrade-bot: upgrade-bot: Canary push completed for seed-2026-03-21-2 — result=partial_apply (resumable)

alex: thanks. will follow up in the PR with the handshake diagram and state machine.

maria: looks good.

jon: add metric names to the PR so dashboards can be sketched early.

ops: ping SRE to schedule an oncall table for when we flip this on in staging.

alex: noted. thanks everyone.
